newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 2.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- Front page story describes activities nationwide to mark Labour day
- Elder statesman Peng Zhen, who died on April 26 aged 95, will be cremated on May 5 in Beijing.
- Wujiang city in eastern Jiangsu province, which has limited arable land, finds new way to boost local economy by increasing its farmland, adds 300 hectares in past eight years.
- China to promote excellent films in May
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- Front page story celebrates 50th anniversary of China's first system of regional autonomy for ethnic minorities in Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.
- Tung Chee Hwa, chief executive of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, attends cocktail reception by Hong Kong Federation of Trade Unions in Hong Kong to mark May Day.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- China begins issue of 40 billion yuan tradeable bonds from May 1
ECONOMIC DAILY
- China machinery industry exports rise in first quarter, industrial output value rises 9.3 percent year-on-year
- Shanghai railway officials hail 1,200 days service without major accident
INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS DAILY
- Tianjin airport becomes major centre for trade with Russia
CHINA DAILY
- Vice-Premier and Foreign Minister Qian Qichen meets U.S. President Bill Clinton, both pledge to improve Sino-U.S. ties
- Tuition-free education for college students to end in remaining 368 free colleges and universities soon after China began charging students fees this year.
- China to focus on spelling out measures to reduce vehicle emissions
- Smog-enveloped Shanghai to spend about $1.0 billion annually on environmental protection.
